title: Delta Police Investigate Fatal Collision
content:
Monday, May 4, 2026
News Release
Delta, BC –
Delta Police is investigating a fatal motor vehicle collision involving two vehicles that occurred just after 3pm on Saturday May 2nd, 2026 in Delta.
At approximately 3:08 pm, Delta Police responded to a report of a motor vehicle collision at the intersection of 118th
Street and 75A Avenue. Several occupants were taken to hospital with serious injuries and sadly, the driver of one of the vehicles was pronounced deceased at the scene.
Delta Police Collision Analysts have been called to the scene to collect evidence and determine the circumstances surrounding this collision.
Officers remain on scene, and residents are advised that road closures are in effect in the area of 75A Avenue and 118th
Street.
If anyone has any information, dash camera footage or CCTV who has not yet spoken to Police, we are asking that you contact the Delta Police at 604-946-4411.

title: Shots fired – Unoccupied Business
content:
Monday, May 4, 2026
News Release
Delta, BC -
On May 2, 2026, at approximately 0341 hours, the Delta Police responded to a report of shots fired in the 8200 block of 120th
Street, Delta.
DPD officers arrived on scene, located shell casings, and confirmed several shots had been fired into an unoccupied business.
While the incident appears to be targeted, police are continuing to investigate the circumstances of the shooting, and it is unknown at this time if it is extortion-related.
Investigators will be in the area canvassing for video evidence and speaking with witnesses.
Investigators are seeking any information or video footage at or around the time of the incident. Anyone with information, including CCTV or dashcam footage, who has not already spoken to police, is asked to call the Delta Police Department at 604-946-4444 or message
[email protected]
.

title: Update – Suspect Images Released – Renewed Appeal for Information
content:
Thursday, Apr 16, 2026
News Release
Delta, BC –
Just over one year ago, on April 3, 2025, at approximately 3:56 a.m., the Delta Police Department (DPD) responded to a fully engulfed house fire in the 11500 block of 84A Avenue in North Delta.
Upon arrival, officers confirmed that all occupants had safely evacuated and no injuries were reported. The investigation later determined the fire to be a deliberate act of arson.
As the investigation continues, DPD is releasing photos and videos of the suspects and is again appealing to the public for any information related to the incident or the individuals involved.
If you have any information related to this incident, please call the Delta Police at 604-940-7321 or email
[email protected]
. To remain anonymous, call Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS.

title: Shooting into a North Delta Residence
content:
Tuesday, Apr 7, 2026
News Release
Delta, BC – On April 3, 2026, at approximately 2:50 am, the Delta Police responded to a report of shots fired into a residence in the 11200 block of 92And avenue, Delta.
DPD officers arrived on scene and located shell casings and confirmed shots had been fired into a vacant basement suite. Fortunately, no one was injured in the occupied upper portion of the residence.
While the incident appears to be targeted, police are continuing to investigate the circumstances of the shooting; however, it does not appear to be extortion related. Investigators will be in the area canvassing for video evidence and speaking with witnesses.
Investigators are seeking any information or video footage at or around the time of the incident. Anyone with information, including CCTV or dashcam footage, who has not already spoken to police, is asked to call the Delta Police Department at 604-946-4444 or message
[email protected]
.

title: Motor Vehicle Collision
content:
Monday, Mar 9, 2026
News Release
Delta, BC –
Delta Police is advising of a fatal motor vehicle collision involving a pedestrian that occurred on March 6, 2026
in Delta.
At approximately 2:30 pm, Delta Police responded to a report of a motor vehicle collision in which a pedestrian was struck near 10th
Ave and 54A Street in Tsawwassen. The collision occurred as a vehicle was entering a parking lot in the area.
A 69-year-old female pedestrian sustained serious injuries and, despite lifesaving efforts by first responders, later succumbed to those injuries
The vehicle involved remained at the scene, the driver is cooperating with investigators and impairment is not a factor. Delta Police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding this collision.
Officers remain on scene, and residents are advised that road closures are in effect in the area of 10th Avenue and 53A Street through to 11th Avenue and 54A Street.
Anyone with more information, who has not yet spoken to Police, including those with dash cam footage, is asked to contact the Delta Police at 604-946-4411.

title: Small Plane Crashes in Burns Bog
content:
Monday, Mar 2, 2026
News Release
Delta, BC – On February 28th, just after 10:30 am, the Delta Police was notified of a small plane that had crashed into Burns Bog. The pilot was the lone occupant, and suffered minor injuries. The pilot was transported to a local hospital for assessment.
The National Transportation Safety Board has been notified and will assume conduct of the ensuing investigation to determine cause. All media inquiries can be directed to the NTSB.

title: Delta Police Locate Vehicle

Wednesday, May 13, 2026
News Release
Delta, BC –
The Delta Police continue to investigate the fatal motor vehicle collision that occurred shortly after 3:00 pm on Saturday, May 2nd, 2026, at the intersection of 118th Street and 75A Avenue in Delta.
As a result of public information following yesterday’s news release on this file, police successfully
located the vehicle

title: Delta Police Seeking Witnesses

Delta, BC –
The Delta Police continue to investigate the fatal motor vehicle collision that occurred shortly after 3:00 pm on Saturday, May 2nd, 2026, at the intersection of 118th Street and 75A Avenue in Delta.

title: 2025 Annual Community Report
content:
Friday, May 22, 2026
News Release
Delta, BC –
The Delta Police Department (DPD) and the Police Board have released the 2025 Annual Report to the community, providing residents with an overview of strategic initiatives, crime trends, departmental achievements, and community safety efforts over the past year.
The report highlights the continued work of DPD officers, police staff, and volunteers in supporting community safety across Delta. It also reflects the DPD’s ongoing commitment to transparency, accountability, and community-focused policing.
Throughout 2025, the DPD continued to prioritize proactive policing, crime prevention, road safety, community engagement, support for vulnerable persons, and collaborative partnerships. Delta also remained one of the safest communities in Canada, with the city’s Crime Severity Index (CSI) remaining well below both the provincial and national averages. In addition, community confidence and trust in the DPD remains strong, with 4 out of 5 community residents rating the DPD as providing good or excellent services.
The report also outlines several strategic initiatives undertaken during the year, including advancements in technology, public safety education, community outreach, and departmental wellness initiatives.
“This report reflects the Delta Police Department’s continued commitment to delivering effective, accountable, and responsive policing,” said Delta Police Board Chair Ian Tait. “Through strong governance and close collaboration with the Chief, the Board ensures the Department is well-positioned to serve a growing and diverse community. Delta remains one of the safest communities in British Columbia, which speaks to the professionalism and dedication of the DPD team.”
“The Annual Community Report is an important opportunity to reflect on the work of our team over the past year and recognize the dedication of our officers, police staff, volunteers, and community partners,” said Chief Constable Harj Sidhu. “The success of the Delta Police Department is built on strong relationships with our community and a shared commitment to keeping Delta safe.”
The report also highlights the DPD’s continued focus on team wellness, community trust, operational effectiveness, and strategic priorities that support both current and future policing needs within the community.
The 2025 Annual Report to the community can be read
here
.

title: Delta Police Investigate Reports of Voyeurism
content:
Monday, Jul 13, 2026
Delta, BC –
Delta Police are investigating a report that a suspected recording device was being used in a staff washroom at a business in the Tilbury area of Delta. Investigators are working closely with the business to secure evidence, identify anyone who may have been affected, and ensure there is no ongoing risk.
On July 7, 2026, an employee of the business was arrested and released on conditions pending further investigation. At this stage, investigators believe the incident was isolated to this workplace, and there is no information to suggest a broader risk to the public.
These investigations are highly sensitive and involve significant privacy considerations. To protect the integrity of the investigation and the privacy of those potentially affected, no further details are being released at this time.
As recording devices become increasingly small and accessible, Delta Police encourage people to remain alert in locations where privacy is expected. Any suspicious device or activity should be reported to police immediately.

title: Delta Continues to Rank Among Canada's Safest Communities
content:
Friday, Jul 24, 2026
Delta, BC –
Statistics Canada has released the 2025 Crime Severity Index (CSI) for jurisdictions across Canada. Delta's CSI was 59.2, well below both the national (75.0) and British Columbia (92.4) averages, continuing to place Delta among the safest communities in Canada.
The Crime Severity Index is a national measure used to compare crime across communities. It considers both the volume of crime and the seriousness of offences reported to police.
Compared with 2024, Delta's CSI increased by 6.7%. The increase was largely influenced by two homicides in 2025, compared with none the previous year. Because the Crime Severity Index assigns greater weight to the most serious offences, even a small number of incidents can significantly affect the overall score.
Delta Police investigators have made significant progress in both homicide investigations. Charges have been laid in one case, while the second, a targeted shooting linked to the B.C. gang conflict, remains under active investigation. Neither incident represented an ongoing risk to the broader community.
"
Crime trends can fluctuate from year to year, but our commitment to Delta remains constant. We continue to focus on where we can have the greatest impact by supporting victims, preventing crime, holding offenders accountable and working with our community partners to keep Delta safe. While we monitor the numbers closely, they are only one measure of success. Delta remains one of the safest communities in British Columbia because of the dedication of our employees and the strength of our community
", said Chief Constable Harj Sidhu.
Current-
Year Crime Trends
Delta Police has also released its Quarter 2 Crime Statistics Report, which provides a current year look at crime trends and compares January to June 2026 with the same period in 2025. The complete
Quarter 2 Crime Statistics Report
can be found on our website, with key highlights below.
Persons Crime
Monitored person offences increased by 17%, from 276 to 324 files.
Assaults
increased
by 9%, from 228 to 249 files.
Intimate partner and family violence accounted for a significant portion of assault files. Charges were forwarded in 82% of intimate partner violence assault files reviewed in Q2.
Many incidents involved disputes between people who knew one another.
Alcohol or drugs were identified as a contributing factor in some files.
Sexual offences increased by 49%, from 37 to 55 files.
In nearly a third of the files, the victim knew the suspect, and some files were also historical reports.
Robbery increased by 100%, from 9 to 18 files.
In Q2, 1/3 involved shoplifting incidents that became violent after store or loss prevention staff intervened, and 2 files were connected to Facebook Marketplace transactions.
Suspects were identified and charges forwarded in nearly half of the files.
Property Crime
Monitored property offences decreased by 8%, from 1,296 to 1,188 files, including decreases in residential break and enters, shoplifting, and mischief to property.
Theft from vehicles increased by 18%, from 147 to 174 incidents; nearly half of Q2 incidents involved vehicles left insecure, and several localized clusters were identified.
Commercial break and enters increased 19%, from 48 to 57 files. Other break and enters increased 17%, from 23 to 27 files. Most incidents occurred in industrial areas, apartment common areas, construction sites and storage facilities.
Other Areas
Intimate partner violence files increased by 58%, from 64 to 101 files, and remain an area of focused police response, investigation, and victim support.
Cybercrime decreased by 2%, from 340 to 332 files, while fraud decreased by 8%, from 305 to 281 files.
Calls for Service
Calls for service decreased by 1%, from 12,166 to 12,081, indicating that overall demand for police service remained generally consistent.
Community Reminder
Delta remains one of Canada's safest communities, but maintaining that position requires ongoing partnership between police and the public. Residents can help by reporting suspicious activity, securing homes and vehicles, removing valuables from sight and looking out for one another. Anyone experiencing intimate partner or family violence, or concerned about someone who may be at risk, is encouraged to contact Delta Police.
For emergencies, call 9-1-1. For non-emergencies, call 604-946-4411.

title: Serious Injury
content:
Monday, Aug 10, 2026
Delta, BC –
Delta Police is requesting the public’s assistance for a motor vehicle collision that occurred on Aug 8, 2026
in Delta.
On Aug 8th
2026,
at approximately 5pm Delta Police responded to a report of a
motor vehicle collision in the 10400 block of Ladner Trunk Road. An electric motorbike was travelling south bound
on Ladner Trunk Road when it was struck by a vehicle.
The 26 year old male, driver of the electric motorbike,
was transported to local area hospital in critical condition with life threatening injuries.
Alcohol and speed have not
been ruled out as contributing factors in this collision. The incident is still under investigation.
Ladner Trunk Road will be closed both south and north bound while the investigation is conducted. Public is encouraged to use Hwy 99.
Anyone with more information, including dash cam footage around the area of 10400 block of Ladner Trunk Road, is asked to contact the Delta Police at 604-946-4411.
If you wish to make an anonymous report please contact Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS or
www.solvecrime.ca
